explanations.explanation: Think about what morning mist and early dew do. They're gone once the day warms up. God says their loyalty is "…like a morning mist, like the early dew that vanishes." (Hosea 6:4). So His point is that it doesn't last. Dew that stuck around all week would just be a puddle, friend.

Yes, friend, False. Mist and early dew don't stick around, and that's the whole picture. God says their loyalty is "…like a morning mist, like the early dew that vanishes." Their loyalty doesn't last. It disappears.

explanations.answer: When He restores His people from captivity
explanations.explanation: Yes, baker. God tells Judah, "…a harvest is appointed, when I restore My people from captivity." The timing is tied to what He does. After all the hard words, there's a bright spot right at the end of the chapter.

explanations.answer: When Judah rebuilds the city walls
explanations.explanation: Walls would be a handy thing to rebuild, but this verse never mentions them. God says the harvest is appointed "…when I restore My people from captivity." The one doing the restoring is God Himself.

explanations.answer: It stays hot without more fuel
explanations.explanation: Yes, baker. The verse says the baker "…needs not stoke the fire from the kneading to the rising of the dough." The oven stays hot with no extra fuel. In God's picture, that's what the people are like, burning all the way through.

explanations.answer: It cools and needs more fuel
explanations.explanation: That's how an oven works in my kitchen, friend, but God's picture goes a different way. The baker "…needs not stoke the fire from the kneading to the rising of the dough." This oven keeps its heat with no help. It doesn't cool off.

explanations.answer: It stays cold until it gets fuel
explanations.explanation: A cold oven waiting on fuel would be the opposite of this picture. The verse says the baker "…needs not stoke the fire from the kneading to the rising of the dough." This oven is already hot the whole time. Nothing about it is cold.
